historicalRecordsPolicy: Stage A, A.1 and A.2 records remain immutable historical evidence. This audit reconciles them through a derived canonical view and does not rewrite their original decisions.

canonicalFamilyView.reason: Perceptible outcomes are a dependency for consequential interaction and recovery semantics.
Failure must remain perceptible, preserve valid state where possible and never report false success.
Asynchronous consequential flows require governed pending/loading semantics before runtime adoption planning.
This is the high-risk human-agency pattern and already depends on TRAMA.STATUS_MESSAGE; Stage B must not begin before its contract is qualified.
Useful cross-product UX semantics, but not a prerequisite for safe Stage B entry if no Stage B slice depends on it.
Must be qualified before any Stage B slice that claims offline/degraded continuity; otherwise it may remain deferred.

exitCriteria.criterion: Canonical reconciliation of Stage A/A.1/A.2 exists without rewriting historical records
All core prerequisite patterns are QUALIFIED
High-risk human-agency decision pattern REVIEW_DECIDE_CONFIRM is QUALIFIED
Any offline/degraded capability claimed by the first Stage B slice has a qualified contract
Stage B scope, adoption order, rollback and product-specific PVIP preservation are separately reviewed
No Stage A.2 audit or qualification implicitly authorizes runtime migration, STABLE promotion or DOS-A1 activation

duplicationAssessment.finding: Qualification records and evidence receipts are intentionally pattern-specific; they should not be collapsed into one mutable source. A derived index may reduce navigation cost without weakening provenance.
duplicationAssessment.action: Introduce a generated/derived Stage A.2 index only after its validator proves it cannot override source qualification records.

constraints: require perceptible pending and outcome semantics
require stale/conflict and double-activation handling where consequential
